extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community: investigators, grant applicants, institutional administrators, and NIH staff
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy updates, resources, and guidance relevant to grant applicants and administrators. Contains brief notices about application formats, data-sharing plan formats, review-process changes, and initiatives to improve research reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential; investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for the new PF5 Collaborative International Research Project award should follow the PF5 award structure and application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements when preparing DMS Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH has issued this new format to standardize and simplify the required elements for Data Management and Sharing Plans for 2026 pilot use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding replication and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications, awards, and NIH research activities should embed replication and reproducibility throughout biomedical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances a commitment to reliability, and NIH has launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise; reliability is described as foundational to public trust and to benefiting patients and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring classification: 'Competitive But Not Discussed' (CBND)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency review-process modifications, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed' to recognize that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes a procedural scoring classification used when applications below a numerical cutoff are still considered competitive but are not discussed during study section review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized peer review under the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer review is centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The consolidation of peer review into CSR is presented as an institutional policy change with initial effects on the peer-review process; applicants should be aware reviews are administered centrally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of NIH Small Business (Seed Fund) Program
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Seed Fund is reinstated and available to innovators, founders, and R&D-driven small companies seeking NIH funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcement of program availability relevant to small business applicants and prospects for SBIR/STTR-type funding opportunities.
